name: RI-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Amo with large financial advantage ($1.85M vs $2K)
No polling or expert ratings, but fundamentals dominate
model.rationale: Gabe Amo holds a heavily Democratic seat with a massive fundraising edge, while Kellie Keenan has raised almost nothing; prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97%. The fundamentals-based margin of roughly 22 points stands with no contrary evidence.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or unexpected outside spending would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rhode Island's first district is a solidly Democratic seat, and first-term incumbent Gabe Amo is running for reelection with every structural advantage. The district leans about twelve points Democratic, and Amo has built a large war chest of roughly $1.85 million, while Republican Kellie Keenan has raised under $13,000 and has only a few thousand dollars on hand. An independent candidate is also on the ballot but lacks visible resources.

No public general-election polling or expert ratings exist for the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals, and those point firmly to Amo. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 97% chance of winning. The expected margin is in the low twenties, consistent with the district's partisan lean plus incumbency and financial advantages.
